# Funding Director for Orgo

> Self-installing, governed business-funding operations co-founder built on a
> pinned Hermes Agent runtime for Orgo or a private Ubuntu host.

Repository: https://github.com/jbellsolutions/funding-director-agent
Human entry point: https://github.com/jbellsolutions/funding-director-agent/blob/main/START-HERE.md
AI setup brief: https://github.com/jbellsolutions/funding-director-agent/blob/main/AGENTS.md

## Setup-agent instructions

1. Read AGENTS.md, START-HERE.md, SECURITY.md, and orgo/deployment.json.
2. Keep credentials, customer files, provider evidence, and paid training only
   on the private target computer.
3. Run scripts/verify.sh before deployment and orgo/verify.sh afterward.
4. Prove one authorized message and read-only integration checks first.
5. Leave every real provider route inactive until current provider evidence and
   its exact destination have been reviewed.
6. Preserve one-time approval for initial submissions and GoHighLevel writes.

## Core map

- README.md: purpose, architecture, products, safety, and installation
- START-HERE.md: nontechnical Orgo setup
- VPS-README.md: self-hosted Ubuntu setup
- docs/TOOLS.md: Funding Machine, GoHighLevel, submission, and browser boundaries
- docs/SKILLS.md: funding operating skills
- docs/A2A.md: authenticated relationship-manager collaboration
- docs/LIVE-PARITY.md: source and runtime lineage
- files/local-packages/funding-director/: deterministic funding core
- policies/permissions.json: machine-readable approval policy
- org/registry.json: single accountable role definition

## Deployment contract

Workspace: AI Guy
Computer: ai-guy-funding-director
Template: system/hermes-agent@1.0.0
Hermes release: v2026.8.31
Hermes version: 0.21.0
Installer: ./orgo/setup.sh
Connections: ./orgo/connect.sh
Verifier: ./orgo/verify.sh

## Safety boundary

External submissions and CRM changes require the exact owner-approved action,
an expiring approval, and receipt verification. Credit pulls, offer acceptance,
signatures, fees, money movement, adverse-action decisions, credential sharing,
and audit deletion remain human-only or denied.
